diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Therefore, the $\bfM$-Lipschitz continuity of the gradient for $F$ is equivalent to the Lipschitz continuity of the gradient for $f$, which is equivalent to 

that $\nabla_z^2 f(z)$, i.e.  $\bfP^\top \nabla_w^2 F(\bfw) \bfP$, has eigenvalues bounded above by $\hat L$.

issues.failure_explanation: For a symmetric Hessian, Lipschitz continuity of the gradient with constant $\hat L$ requires the operator norm to be at most $\hat L$, equivalently every eigenvalue must lie in $[-\hat L,\hat L]$. Merely bounding eigenvalues above allows arbitrarily large negative eigenvalues and therefore does not imply Lipschitz continuity. The repeated lemma has the same defect.

$\iff$ all eigenvalues of $\bfP^\top\nabla^2F(\bfw)\bfP$ are $\le \hat L$;

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the upper-eigenvalue condition by an absolute-eigenvalue/operator-norm bound, or explicitly state only the one-sided Hessian condition needed for a descent upper bound.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed equivalence and the paper's unrestricted spectral interpretation of metric smoothness are false for nonconvex objectives.
issues.title: Spectral characterization of Lipschitz gradients omits absolute eigenvalue bounds
issues.why_classification: This is a short local correction to the spectral characterization and does not alter the convergence theorems, which separately assume metric Lipschitz continuity.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Theorem~\ref{1stmainthm} shows that, with a fixed learning rate $\overline\alpha$,
preconditioned SGD contracts linearly with factor $1-\overline\alpha\,\hat c\,\mu$ and
converges to an asymptotic floor
and in particular $\mathbb E[F(\bw_k)-F_\ast\mid\tau=\infty]\to C$ as $k\to\infty$.

issues.failure_explanation: The recursion proves only an upper bound whose right-hand side tends to the displayed floor. It implies at most a limsup bound, not that the expected gap itself converges to that value. For example, the assumptions permit a loose positive choice of $K$ even when the actual gradients are deterministic and the gap converges to zero.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace convergence-to-floor assertions by $\limsup$ upper bounds and describe the displayed quantity as an upper bound on the asymptotic error.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted equality of the asymptotic loss with the nominal noise floor is unsupported in both fixed-step theorems; the quantity is only a certified upper floor.
issues.title: Upper bounds are misreported as convergence to the noise floor
issues.why_classification: The established finite-time upper bounds and rates remain intact; only the unsupported equality interpretation must be weakened.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Multiply \eqref{eq:stopped-one-step} by $\mathbf 1_{\Omega_\infty}$ and take expectations; since $\mathbf 1_{\Omega_\infty}\mathbf 1_{\{k<\tau\}}=\mathbf 1_{\Omega_\infty}$,

and, on the event $\{\tau=\infty\}$, we have the conditional rate
\[
  \mathbb{E}\!\left[F(\bw_k)-F_\ast \mid \tau=\infty\right] \;\le\; \frac{\nu}{\gamma + k}
  \qquad \forall\,k\ge1.
\]

issues.failure_explanation: The event $\Omega_\infty=\{\tau=\infty\}$ depends on the current and all future gradient noise and is not $\mathcal F_k$-measurable. A conditional drift inequality given $\mathcal F_k$ therefore cannot be restricted to that event, nor can it be multiplied by its indicator before taking expectations, without changing the conditional distribution of $g_k$. Survival can select atypical noise trajectories. In addition, the theorem allows the stated lower bound on $\mathbb P(\Omega_\infty)$ to be zero, in which case the conditional expectation is not even defined.

failure_location.quote:
Then, on the event $\{\tau=\infty\}$, the iterates exhibit conditional geometric convergence in expectation to the noise floor $C$: for all $k\ge1$,
\[
  \mathbb{E}\!\big[F(\bw_k)-F_\ast \,\big|\, \tau=\infty\big]
  \;\le\;
  C \;+\;
  (1-\rho)^{k-1}\bigl(F(\bw_1)-F_\ast - C\bigr),
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must control the change of law induced by conditioning on eternal survival and ensure that this event has positive probability, or replace the conditional guarantees with rigorously derived stopped/killed-process guarantees.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised conditional geometric and $O(1/k)$ convergence guarantees inside the local basin are not established. This defeats the central local convergence component of both local theorems, though it does not by itself refute a correctly proved stopped-process or exit-probability bound.
issues.title: Conditioning on eternal basin survival invalidates the local rate recursions
issues.why_classification: The invalid step is the core architecture for both local rate claims. Repairing it requires a new conditional-survival argument or a material change in guarantee type.

issues.failure_explanation: Subtracting $C$ from the displayed inequality gives an additional term $\rho C(1-\mathbf 1_{\{k<\tau\}})$, so the asserted supermartingale inequality does not follow. The error results from replacing the noise term's stopping indicator by one and then treating it as though the indicator remained.

failure_location.quote:
Define $Y_k:=F(\widetilde{\bw}_k)-F_\ast - C$. Then \eqref{eq:cond-step} implies
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[Y_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k\right]
\le (1-\rho\,\mathbf 1_{\{k<\tau\}})\,Y_k,
\]
so $(Y_{k\wedge\tau})_{k\ge1}$ is a supermartingale.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain $\mathbf 1_{\{k<\tau\}}$ on the $K$ term throughout the stopped descent calculation; then the shifted recursion has the required indicator and the optional-stopping argument can proceed.
issues.overall_effect: The optional-stopping derivation of the fixed-step basin-stability probability is unsupported as written.
issues.title: The fixed-step stability proof asserts a supermartingale after dropping the stopping indicator
issues.why_classification: The source already contains the sharper indicator-bearing inequality before relaxing it, so a short local correction restores the stability proof without changing its bound.

issues.failure_explanation: Strong convexity implies uniqueness of the minimizer, but uniqueness does not imply strong convexity; for instance, a function can have a unique minimizer while having zero curvature there. Thus the claimed equivalence is false.

issues.title: Unique minimization is incorrectly claimed equivalent to strong convexity
issues.why_classification: A one-line weakening corrects the claim and leaves every theorem and guarantee unchanged.
